Build a Data-Driven Lambda Grid for the Ordinal Learner (Experimental)

auto_ordinal_lambda_grid.Rd

Builds the ordinal analog of auto_lambda_grid(): one ordinalNet cumulative-logit model with parallel terms is fit on the full data, and the grid is taken from its decreasing lambda path. The grid is computed once on the full data; each bootstrap subsample is subsequently fit at these fixed penalties with its own model.

Usage

auto_ordinal_lambda_grid(x, y, n_lambda = 30L, alpha = 1)

Arguments

x

A matrix or data.frame of features (samples in rows).

y

Factor outcome; the level order is the band order. An ordered factor is recommended.

n_lambda

Positive integer; number of lambda values. Default 30L.

alpha

Numeric in (0, 1]; the elastic-net mixing weight. Default 1 (pure lasso).

Value

A data.frame with a single lambda column, sorted in decreasing order so the path runs sparse-to-dense, matching the convention used by stabl_fit().

See also

make_ordinal_adapter(), auto_lambda_grid(), stabl_fit()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ordinalNet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1L)
  x <- matrix(rnorm(400L), 40L, 10L,
              dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("f", 1:10)))
  eta <- x[, 1] - 0.5 * x[, 2]
  y   <- cut(eta + rnorm(40L, sd = 0.5), breaks = 4,
             labels = paste0("L", 1:4), ordered_result = TRUE)
  grid <- auto_ordinal_lambda_grid(x, y, n_lambda = 5L)
  head(grid)
}
#>        lambda
#> 1 0.340240255
#> 2 0.107593416
#> 3 0.034024025
#> 4 0.010759342
#> 5 0.003402403
